definitions.explanation: A type of thick, chewy wheat flour noodle commonly used in Japanese cuisine, typically served in hot broth or cold with dipping sauce.

examples.japanese: {冷|つめ}たいうどんが{食|た}べたい。
examples.english: I want to eat cold udon.

examples.japanese: うどんをつるつる{食|た}べる。
{讃岐|さぬき}うどんは{香川県|かがわけん}の{名物|めいぶつ}だ。
examples.english: Sanuki udon is a specialty of Kagawa Prefecture.

examples.japanese: {寒|さむ}い{日|ひ}は{温|あたた}かいうどんが{食|た}べたくなる。
examples.english: On cold days, I crave warm udon.

examples.japanese: お{昼|ひる}に{駅前|えきまえ}のうどん{屋|や}に{行|い}って、{天|てん}ぷらうどんを{食|た}べた。
examples.english: At lunchtime I went to the udon shop in front of the station and had tempura udon.

notes:
うどん is one of the most popular traditional Japanese noodle dishes, made from wheat flour. The noodles are thick and chewy, in contrast to the thinner そば (buckwheat noodles).

COMMON TYPES:
- {掛|か}けうどん: udon in hot broth (the simplest style)
- {釜揚|かまあ}げうどん: freshly boiled udon with dipping sauce
- ざるうどん: cold udon served on a bamboo tray
- {焼|や}きうどん: stir-fried udon
- {天|てん}ぷらうどん: udon topped with tempura

CULTURE:
{讃岐|さぬき}うどん from {香川県|かがわけん} is the most famous regional variety. Udon shops ({うどん{屋|や}}) are widespread and serve as affordable, quick meal spots.

RELATED WORDS:
- そば: buckwheat noodles (thinner, often paired as a comparison)
- ラーメン: ramen (Chinese-origin wheat noodles in flavored broth)
- {素麺|そうめん}: very thin wheat noodles, usually eaten cold in summer
